issues.description: The problem description contains conflicting specifications for the Farm.animals collection: the UML in the problem statement declares animals as List<Animal>, while the textual Part 3 instructs students to use a Set implemented with HashSet to enforce unique animals. The provided solution implements animals as a List (ArrayList). This mismatch (UML vs. textual instructions vs. solution) creates confusion about which collection type students must use and may cause them to implement the wrong data structure or fail tests that expect uniqueness.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the intended collection type consistent across all artifacts. Either (A) update the problem UML and textual description to require a List (and adjust the text that mentions HashSet), and keep the solution using List/ArrayList; or (B) follow the textual instruction to require a Set and update the UML and the solution/template Farm.java to declare and initialize animals as a Set<Animal> (e.g., private Set<Animal> animals = new HashSet<>();), and update getter/setter and usage accordingly. Prefer option B if uniqueness is pedagogically intended.

issues.description: The collection type used to hold Farm animals is inconsistent across artifacts. The problem text explicitly requires using a Set (HashSet) for the Farm aggregation to ensure unique animals, while the solution implements a List backed by an ArrayList. The UML in the problem also shows animals: List<Animal>, creating conflicting guidance. This mismatch can confuse students about whether to implement Farm with a Set/HashSet or a List/ArrayList and which behavior (uniqueness vs. allowing duplicates) is required.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the collection type consistent across all artifacts. Either (A) update the solution and UML to use Set<Animal> and initialize it with a HashSet in the Farm constructor (and use Set semantics in addAnimal/feedAllAnimals/singFarmSong), or (B) change the problem text to require a List/ArrayList and remove the instruction to use a HashSet. Prefer aligning solution and template to the explicit textual requirement (use HashSet) and update the UML to show Set<Animal> to avoid mixed signals.
